You are a fix worker on the OBE podcast repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast - edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, branch, or push; leave changes uncommitted. No skills/MCP/network. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.

CONTEXT (live proof-run evidence, episode 2026-06-10-fred-cho, render of 2026-07-23 11:12): the angle-switch publishable render now completes (129 segments, seekable composite) and the TRUE-BOUNDARY time map is built from actual encoded durations (sidecar processed/angle_switched.mp4.boundaries.json), but the transfer gate (media_gates.validate_transfer, mode=av_anchors, threshold 40ms) FAILS with oscillating audio drift at high anchor confidence (0.90-0.99): anchor 0.4s -> -24.0ms (pass), 472.5s -> +47.5ms FAIL (0.023s from a seam), 944.6s -> -41.0ms FAIL (9s from any seam), 1416.8s -> +8.5ms pass, 1888.9s -> -136.5ms FAIL (15s from any seam). DIAGNOSIS: the program AUDIO is assembled per-segment - each segment ffmpeg carries '-map 0:a:0 -af asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS ... -shortest', so every segment's audio is snapped/truncated against its video length (AAC framing + -shortest), 129 snapped scraps are concatenated, and cfr_timeline_clean_cmd then runs '-af aresample=async=1:first_pts=0' which pads/trims audio at every discontinuity - locally stretching audio and leaving oscillating map-vs-audio offsets. The video path and the map are fine; the audio construction is the defect.

TASK: make the angle-switch program audio a SINGLE sample-accurate pass instead of concatenated per-segment scraps.

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: server/pipeline/angle_render.py, server/pipeline/video_assembly.py, tests/test_angle_render.py, tests/test_video_assembly.py. Never modify anything else. Do NOT touch server/pipeline/media_gates.py or any gate threshold - the gate is correct and must be satisfied, not loosened.

BUILD (in angle_render.render_angle_switch and its helpers):
1. Segment renders become VIDEO-ONLY (drop '-map 0:a:0', the -af, audio codec args and '-shortest' from per-segment commands; keep video args incl. -g 60 via the existing helpers). Seam bridges likewise video-only.
2. After video concat, build the FULL program audio in ONE ffmpeg filter pass over the source composite audio: for each kept span in the final applied plan (the same spans the video segments came from, in order) atrim that span from the composite's audio, asetpts continuous, and join with the concat filter; where consecutive segments have a CONTENT-CUT seam with dissolve length d (the same _seam_dissolves values the video used), overlap the neighbors with acrossfade of the same d so audio and video dissolve identically; contiguous camera-switch seams join with plain concat (no gap, no fade). Source spans for audio must be the PLANNED source spans; the edited-timeline positions come from the ACTUAL video segment durations (the true-boundary map) - derive the audio timeline from that map so audio lands where the video actually is, not where the plan predicted. If actual video duration differs from the planned span by more than half a frame, trim/pad that span's audio tail by the difference (atrim to the actual length) so per-segment error cannot accumulate.
3. Mux: program = concatenated video stream + the single-pass audio (aac 192k 48k stereo), '-shortest' only at the final mux.
4. cfr_timeline_clean_cmd: audio is now continuous - replace 'aresample=async=1:first_pts=0' with a non-time-warping chain (e.g. 'aresample=first_pts=0,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS'); it must never insert or drop samples to hide upstream gaps. Keep its video path unchanged. (It is also used by the solo keep-timeline path whose apply_keep_timeline already renders audio in one filter_complex pass - confirm that path still passes its tests with the new -af.)
5. Keep the true-boundary map + boundaries sidecar + edit_plan_receipt exactly as they are.

TESTS (add to owned test files):
(a) executed drift proof: build a synthetic ~60s 1280x720/30fps source whose audio is silence with short 1kHz beeps at known source times (ffmpeg lavfi sine+volume gating or concat of tone/silence spans); apply an edit plan with >=6 kept segments including >=2 content-cut seams with dissolves and >=2 camera switches; render via render_angle_switch; locate each beep in the OUTPUT audio (parse ffmpeg silencedetect or astats over windows) and assert each lands within 15ms of the position predicted by the true-boundary map. This test must FAIL on the old per-segment audio path (state in the summary how you confirmed that, e.g. by running it once before your change).
(b) unit: per-segment render commands contain no '-map 0:a:0' and no '-shortest'; the final mux command carries exactly one audio input; cfr clean cmd contains no 'async=1'.
(c) all existing tests in the four owned files stay green; update any that asserted per-segment audio args and list them in the summary.

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_angle_render.py tests/test_video_assembly.py tests/test_video_assembly_bumpers.py tests/test_keep_timeline.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
